name: West Ridge
rappels: One ~100 ft rappel partway up the route (off a tower into a notch, between pitches 7 and 8); descent is via the separate southeast face route, not by rappelling the ridge
descent_text: From the summit, downclimb the southeast face, including a sprint across a snowfield exposed to rockfall (the FA party noted this crossing would be more straightforward earlier in the season, with more snow cover), circling back to the bivy camp under Ghost Peak.
approach: An involved two-day approach: ~10 miles on trail up and over Hannegan Pass, wading the Chilliwack River, traversing the scenic 5-mile Easy Ridge, soloing exposed 4th-class terrain across the 'Imperfect Impasse,' climbing through Perfect Pass and over the Challenger Glacier, then descending and traversing steep snow, talus, and more glacier to a bivy site under Ghost Peak (Phantom Peak's neighbor immediately to the north), from which the full west ridge comes into view.
overview: A 2021 first ascent up Phantom Peak's previously-unclimbed west ridge: ten pitches of mostly sustained 5.7+ ridge climbing (one 5.10-ish crux stemming move over an airy gap) from a 6,100' saddle, finishing with about 400 ft of 4th-class soloing to the summit.
beta: From a roping-up ledge just above the 6,100' saddle in the ridge's lower reaches, pitch 1 starts with a short, steep crack system before rambling along the crest. Pitches 2-5 continue in the same vein — large corners, towers either bypassed or climbed directly, and exposed ridge running, mostly 5.7+. Pitch 6 holds the crux: a tough move over an airy four-foot-wide cleft, requiring a long 5.10-ish stemming move across a 100-ft-deep gap (the FA party rigged a nut-and-sling handhold to tension across, then top-roped it free). At the top of pitch 7 the ridge tops out on a tower, from which the party rappelled ~100 ft into a notch; pitches 8-10 offer aesthetic face and crack climbing on solid rock. As the difficulty eases, the rope is coiled and about 400 ft of 4th-class terrain is soloed to the sharp summit ridge, finishing with an exposed traverse to the final summit pinnacle.
gear: Standard alpine trad rack (cams and nuts)
Ice axe and crampons for the Challenger Glacier and steep snow crossings; approach shoes or light boots for the 4th-class sections
